column1: # Every Sassembly program in this repository, classified — task `F-001d`,
# `F-001` promises "apps that run in the browser and outside it". This file was
# the measurement behind ADR-0015's answer to the other half of that sentence —
# **there is no application here** — and since `F-001e3` there is exactly one.
# 47 of the 48 programs are OS proofs, and the `clause` column names the first
# clause of ADR-0015 each one fails. `atithi.sas` fails none, so its clause is
#   A1  entered by a loader, not by a machine reset
#   A2  runs in U-mode and never leaves it
#   A3  calls an application ABI, not SBI
#   A4  writes to a surface it was handed, not to a device
#   A5  its exit leaves the machine running
# Columns after `clause` are DERIVED FROM THE SOURCE, not typed:
#   privileged  names a family `spec/mnemonics-riscv64.src.tsv` marks S or Zicsr
#               — csrrw, csrrs, csrrc, sfence.vma, sret. It is the supervisor.
#   ecall       contains आज्ञापनम्. From S-mode that is an SBI call, and SBI is
#   address     builds a constant with उपरिभारः from a hexadecimal literal. In
#               this tree that is always a device address or a device's magic
#               value — the UART at 0x10000000, the finisher at 0x100000.
#   checks      the `tools/check-*.sh` that reference the file, or — for the
#               application, which is loaded rather than booted and so has no
#               QEMU check to be run under — `crates/yantra/tests/application.rs`.
#               Every program has at least one: each exists to be asserted about.
# `crates/yantra/tests/application.rs` re-derives all four columns and the
# clause, and fails if this table disagrees with the source.
# THE CLAUSE COLUMN IS SOURCE-DERIVED AND A3 IS NOT IN IT. A2 and A4 are refusals
# a reader can make from the text; A3 is not, because the same `a7` means
# (`spec/application-abi.tsv`), and nothing in a source says which privilege will
# execute it. So a boot proof's clause is derived from its text, and the
# application's claim is carried by RUNNING it: the loader places it, the machine
# reports `scause` 8, the supervisor answers both calls, the bytes land on the
# granted surface, the UART stays empty, and the machine hosts a second program
# afterwards. That is what the word `app` costs here, and it is why a row cannot
# WHAT THE `checks` COLUMN MEANS, EXACTLY: asserted about by a `tools/check-*.sh`,
# or by `crates/yantra/tests/application.rs`. The scanner in that file reads those
# and nothing else, so a Rust test asserting about a program does not appear here
# programs and is in no row (`B-058b2b7`). An empty-looking column is a limit of
# the scanner, not evidence that nothing checks the program.
